idempotency.verified_at: The ingestDatamap tool description published by https://api.noru.tech/v1/mcp reads: "Ingest a Fideslang privacy manifest (parsed .fides/datamap.yml) for a source. Idempotent: identical content is a no-op." It documents `slug` as "Stable source identifier, unique per org (e.g. noru-tech/app)." That covers the case this piece actually re-runs in: CI on an unchanged repository pushes the same manifest and nothing changes. It does not cover the changed-content path — see `gap`. https://api.noru.tech/llms.txt confirms the scope verbatim (`write:datamaps` — "Push fideslang privacy manifests (`.fides/datamap.yml`) from CI"), but its "Idempotency/Upsert Behavior" section names only POST /v1/assets and POST /v1/security-findings, and the document publishes no REST endpoint for datamap ingestion at all. So there is one public source for this behaviour, not two.
idempotency.gap: What is documented is a no-op on identical content, not an upsert on `slug`. Nothing public says what happens when the same slug is pushed with a CHANGED manifest — replaced, merged, or filed alongside as a second record — and that is the ordinary case, because the manifest changes every time the schema does. Until it is documented, `:diff` reads getPrivacyDataMap and listPrivacyDatasets first and the piece shows the change set rather than asserting what the server will do with it. A documented upsert on `slug` would let this be declared server_upsert — the shape requirement 4 asks for — and would let the pre-read go.

source.note: The schemas, models, migrations and API contracts the repository actually contains. This half of the queue is repo-resident truth: no server-side integration can see which columns exist on a branch that has not merged, and no API key can read a migration.

The vocabulary Noru itself holds. The bundled snapshot under references/taxonomy/ is the offline floor required by requirement 3; where the piece can reach Noru it reconciles against this and reports a difference rather than silently preferring what is on disk.
What the organization's data map already says, so :diff shows a real change set instead of reporting an established data map as entirely new.
The datasets Noru already holds for this source, so a collection that moved between stores reads as a move rather than as a deletion and an unrelated creation.

exit_codes.1: drift, validation failure, an unresolved needs_review claim, or a stale plan
exit_codes.2: usage error, including a push without --confirm

outputs.purpose: The data map in Ethyca's own on-disk format, for the `fides` CLI and anything else that reads a Fides manifest. It is not the manifest: `.noru/privacy-datamap.yml` carries the citations, the attribution and the review state, and is what `:push` is bound to; this is that content projected down to plain Fideslang with the piece's own bookkeeping removed. Keeping the conventional path is the whole point — a data map the ecosystem's tooling cannot read is a data map that only Noru can use.
